stories.headline: Israeli election ends in deadlock as Netanyahu and opposition stall while Arab parties gain
stories.body:
Israeli political leaders faced a deadlock on Wednesday after election results left neither major group with a majority.

With nearly 90 percent of the votes counted by Wednesday evening, neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot had enough seats to form a government on his own. A majority in the 120-seat Israeli parliament, called the Knesset, requires 61 seats. Early results put the coalition bloc of Benjamin Netanyahu at about 53 to 54 seats. The bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot stood at around 49 seats. Netanyahu's Likud party remains the largest single party in the parliament, with an estimated 26 seats. Eisenkot formed his political party, called Yashar, one year before the 2026 election.

Arab citizens of Israel turned out to vote in record numbers during this election. Overall voter turnout on October 27 was the highest recorded in Israel since 1999. Arab citizens make up approximately 20 percent of the population in Israel, which is roughly 2.1 million people. The two main Arab parties in the country are projected to win around 19 of the 120 seats in the Knesset. These two main Arab political parties are the Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, and Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas.

Yousef Jabareen said that the Joint List would seek to use its projected 12 seats to help remove the government of Benjamin Netanyahu. Mansour Abbas said that senior members of Eisenkot's bloc had discussed a potential coalition deal with him before the election took place. Eisenkot said he wants an Israeli government that is Zionist and committed to universal military service. Yair Golan, the leader of the centre-left Democrats party, called for creating a change government in partnership with Arab citizens of Israel. In Tel Aviv, Israelis held rallies demanding a Jewish-Arab government after Arab parties made major gains in Tuesday's election.

Likud spokesman Guy Levy confirmed that Likud would not negotiate with any Arab party to form a government. In addition, the Central Elections Committee received a complaint from the Likud party. The complaint alleged that Arab parties compromised election integrity.

United Nations rights chief Volker Turk expressed his views on the political outcome. Turk said he hopes the next Israeli government will change course massively and respect international law. The Israeli Knesset is scheduled to open on November 10.

stories.headline: Defeated Brazilian candidate Flávio Bolsonaro arrives in Florida after leaving Brazil
stories.body:
Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro landed at Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport in Florida after leaving Brazil in secret. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who won the runoff election by over four million votes, called the departure a shameful act. Bolsonaro's political party acknowledged the official election results.

Bolsonaro wrote in a letter that he did not flee Brazil but left for the sake of Brazil. He posted on social media calling himself the elected president before changing the word to leader. In the letter, he thanked Argentine President Javier Milei and US President Donald Trump. Trump said he would not get involved, calling the election very strange.

Bolsonaro traveled by land into Argentina, took a private jet from Puerto Iguazú, stopped in Ecuador, and flew to Miami. Brazilian authorities canceled his passports after he missed a 24-hour deadline to hand them in. Federal police faced criticism for failing to stop him.

Bolsonaro faces criminal investigation in Brazil over financial crimes, corruption, and money laundering linked to an unreleased film called Dark Horse. He loses his parliamentary immunity in February. He has held Italian nationality since 2023. His father Jair Bolsonaro is in jail for conspiring to stay in power.

Newly re-elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won the runoff election by more than four million votes.

US President Donald Trump told reporters regarding the Brazilian election: 'I won't get involved. It was a very strange election, that's for sure.'
Flávio Bolsonaro and his family travelled by land into Argentina, boarded a private jet in Puerto Iguazú, stopped in Guayaquil, Ecuador, and flew on to Miami.
Brazilian authorities cancelled Flávio Bolsonaro's passports after he failed to surrender them within a 24-hour deadline.
Brazil's federal police faced public criticism for failing to prevent Flávio Bolsonaro from leaving the country.
Flávio Bolsonaro is under criminal investigation in Brazil over financial crimes, corruption, and money laundering related to the unreleased film 'Dark Horse'.
Flávio Bolsonaro is scheduled to lose his parliamentary immunity from prosecution in February when his Senate term expires.
Flávio Bolsonaro has held Italian nationality since 2023.
Former president Jair Bolsonaro is in jail in Brazil on charges of leading a conspiracy to stay in power after losing the 2022 election.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab hits eastern India, killing several people and displacing thousands
stories.body:
Severe cyclonic storm Arnab hit the eastern coast of India, causing deaths, heavy rain, and damage across several states.

The storm crossed the coasts of Andhra Pradesh and Yanam early on Wednesday. It made landfall about 20 kilometers east-northeast of Narsapur as a very severe cyclonic storm. At its peak, sustained wind speeds reached 125 to 135 kilometers per hour, with gusts up to 150 kilometers per hour. The India Meteorological Department stated that the storm later weakened into a deep depression. Forecasters expect it to weaken further into a depression on Thursday morning, October 29, 2026.

Reports differed on the exact number of deaths caused by the storm in Andhra Pradesh. The Times of India reported that eight people died in parts of the state after the storm crossed the coast. NDTV reported five deaths from fallen trees and electrocution, with single deaths in Visakhapatnam, Anakapalle, Kakinada, Konaseema, and West Godavari districts. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu also stated that five people died. Scroll.in reported that three people died in the state as the storm made landfall. Scroll.in added that the storm damaged 31 houses.

Before the cyclone arrived, authorities moved more than 20,000 people out of coastal districts in Andhra Pradesh. Heavy rain fell across the region. Garividi in Vizianagaram district recorded 26 centimeters of rain between Tuesday morning and Wednesday morning. This was the highest rainfall recorded in Andhra Pradesh. The India Meteorological Department issued a flash flood warning for 13 districts in Andhra Pradesh and Yanam until Thursday morning.

Chief Minister Naidu announced a relief and compensation package for affected residents. He spoke to Union Home Minister Amit Shah to ask for central help for damaged crops and infrastructure. The neighboring Telangana government offered full support and emergency personnel to help Andhra Pradesh restore power and deliver relief.

Neighboring states also felt the impact of the cyclone. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said heavy rain affected at least 17 districts in southern Odisha. Ahead of the storm, Odisha authorities moved about 28,000 people to relief camps. They also relocated 2,200 pregnant women to safe places. In Chhattisgarh, officials ordered all educational institutions in Raipur district to close on Thursday due to heavy rain and strong wind forecasts.

stories.headline: India confirms 22 citizens killed in West Asia conflict zone since February
stories.body:
Indian officials confirmed that 22 Indian citizens have died in the West Asia conflict zone. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the deaths include 14 seafarers. He added that India maintains strong ties with Israel and will work to strengthen them.

The conflict expanded after the United States and Israel launched military strikes on Iran on February 28. Those strikes killed Iran's supreme leader and senior officials. The United States launched fresh attacks on July 9 after President Donald Trump declared an interim ceasefire was over.

In Saudi Arabia, three Indian nationals died in incidents linked to regional tensions. The Indian Consulate General in Jeddah issued a travel advisory listing extra flights by airlines such as Flynas to help citizens and Umrah pilgrims.

At sea, three Indian seafarers named Aditya Sharma, Shivanand Chaurashiya, and Patnala Suresh died on June 9. A United States strike hit their Palau-flagged tanker, the MT Settebello, off Oman. In July, Iranian missiles struck the Emirati oil tankers Mombasa and Al Bahiyah in Omani waters. That attack killed one Indian sailor and injured six others.

Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that India has strong relations with Israel and will work to further improve and strengthen those ties.
The United States and Israel launched military strikes on Iran on February 28, killing Iran's supreme leader and senior officials.
The United States military launched fresh attacks on Iran on July 9 after President Donald Trump declared that an interim ceasefire was over.

The Consulate General of India in Jeddah issued a travel advisory detailing expanded flight schedules by carriers such as Flynas to assist Indian nationals and Umrah pilgrims.

stories.headline: Supreme Court scrutinises Election Commission over voter list removals across India
stories.body:
The Supreme Court of India urged the Election Commission not to force removed Delhi voters to reapply as new voters. Judges said nearly 4.3 million removed electors should not use Form 6 if they were on the 2026 rolls. Out of about 14.5 million electors at the start of Delhi's revision, around 4.7 million did not submit forms.

The court stated it had not approved the commission's logical discrepancy label. That classification previously removed 2.71 million people from voter rolls in West Bengal. In a May 27 judgment, the court ruled the revision process met proportionality rules and obeyed election law.

The national voter revision began in Bihar in June 2025. By September 1, about 13.37 crore names were missing from draft rolls across India. Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi formally objected 14 times in 10 months to actions taken during the exercise.

In Karnataka, about 64.5 lakh voters were missing from final rolls, lowering the total to 45,500,011. Young adults aged 18 to 29 made up 59.5 percent, or 38.41 lakh, of those missing Karnataka voters.
